The surface morphology of dry terpolymer films prepared by solution casting (SC) and electrospraying (ES) were analyzed using SEM (Figure 2). The ES films (Figure 2a) were found to appear more uniform and smoother than the SC films (Figure 2b). The layer-by- layer deposition and rapid solvent evaporation that occurs during electrospray processing are thought to lead to the smoother and more uniform film appearance for ES films. “Crater” features and rougher textures observed on the SC surface may be due to a slower solvent evaporation rate that can cause drying defects,21–23 while the layer-by-layer deposition from ES films could limit the amount of solvent with a rapid evaporation rate on each layer. The film preparation method also affects the thickness consistency of the thin films. Using terpolymer films (1 inch x 1 inch) prepared by ES and SC, film thickness was measured every 0.25 inches using FIB. The ES film (Figure 2c) was found to display a thickness range of 400 nm, while the SC film displayed a thickness range of 1600 nm for a film of the same size (Figure 2d). Electrosprayed films (Figure 2e) were smoother than solution casted films (Figure 2f) as measured using atomic force microscopy (AFM). The root mean square (RMS) roughness from a film with area of 20 µm x 20 µm was 15.4  1.7 nm for ES and 135.7  19.4 nm for SC. In addition to increased uniformity, fabricating films by electrospraying is faster than solution casting. For example, to generate a thin film with a thickness of 5 µm, DMF takes about 24h to evaporate completely when solution casted, whereas electrospraying takes less than an hour to create the terpolymer thin film. Therefore, electrospray processing, as a faster thin film fabrication method, is a promising method for the generation of electrocaloric thin films.
